Comp AI CRM is an open source, CRM designed for AI agents. Agentic-first CRM.

The agent · Stack · Quick start · Configuration · Deploying · Contributing

Most CRMs are a database with a form in front of it. The AI ones bolt a chat box onto the side of that form. Both leave the actual work — finding out what is true, and writing it down — to a human who has better things to do.

stories.title: The Mythology of Conscious AI
stories.body: Why consciousness is more likely a property of life than of computation and why creating conscious, or even conscious-seeming AI, is a bad idea.

views.text: Consciousness in others isn’t something we prove. It is something we grant and we should be very careful about whom or what we grant it to.
views.author: andsoitis

views.text:
The biggest flaw in this piece is claiming Turing machines cannot exceed the Halting Problem and then reaching for alternative models of computation (in electromagnetic field interactions, in biology, attractors, etc.)... none of which presumably have the power to solve the Halting problem either. Ergo, he is inside "Turing world" without realizing it, while decrying the "poverty" of the Universal Turing Machine.

Ergo, more philosophers should retake undergrad theoretical CS before writing…

views.text:
how dare he tell us we cannot make a computer out of cheese

personally I think conscious AI will be unavoidable because there will be benefits to consciousness. evolution probably selected conscious entities for some fitness reason
views.author: bionhoward

discussion.text:
> Why consciousness is more likely a property of life than of computation

This is a false dichotomy and the first branch is clearly false, since most life (bacteria and insects, by mass, numbers, or species) isn't conscious.

And neither "life" nor "consciousness" are scientific terms with fixed definitions. If we encountered something that was clearly conscious in our judgment, we would likely expand the definition life in whatever way we needed to in order to encompass it.

Anil Seth has made the arguments in TFA many times and they have been rebutted many times.
discussion.author: jibalt

discussion.text:
If you are interested in consciousness, and also interested in going beyond the usual philosophical approach, you might like our book Journey of the Mind https://www.goodreads.com/en/book/show/60500189-journey-of-t...

One thing that is implicit, which I now think we really should have expanded on in the book, is that consciousness is fundamentally an engineering problem.
discussion.author: ChaitanyaSai

discussion.text: Consciousness might not necessarily emerge when there is enough computation, but we also don't know that it doesn't emerge. We really know almost nothing about consciousness. It's possible that the question of why the presence of consciousness is correlated with certain kinds of material organization is in principle not accessible to scientific investigation. We don't even know that it is so correlated in general, we just know that for example people report being conscious when they are not asleep and not drugged in certain ways, and report having had no experience of consciousness during…
discussion.author: hax0ron3

discussion.text: It’s a silly debate when we don’t even know what consciousness is, let alone the circumstances for its occurrence. Or am I missing something?

stories.title: The Birds of GTA 6: A Field Guide to Vice City and Leonida's Wildlife
stories.body: Inside the hunt to catalog the birds of GTA 6. Explore a field guide to Leonida's species, how the birdwatching mechanics play, and how accurate Rockstar's wildlife really is.

discussion.text: I like to imagine that Rockstar was able to pay an ornithologist from Cornell to help them with their birds.
discussion.author: bob1029

discussion.text: The game appears to be mostly story/character focused rather than sandbox focused, despite the insane attention to detail on traditional sandbox elements (for context, I've already completed the main campaign). In a lot of ways it feels like two disjoint teams worked to create the final product and the story/character team won out. Not sure if that's ultimately the root cause of the stated inconsistencies, but it could be a contributing factor.

Just a reminder not to take the progress bar here as an indication that the proof is largely correct, as it takes only one hole for the entire thing to come crashing down.

Judging by other commentary so far, my understanding is that there is a major hole in this proof, which would not surprise me given that the machinery involved feels far less like a major leap (to me anyway) than the route for the Alpoge proof. The asymptotic-order theta lifting in that proof feels like a genuine step forward for other mathematical disciplines.
